---
title: "8. Frequency response"
subtitle: "Read gain, phase, and complex-plane behavior together"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../../AmberMakie/docs"]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!()
set_theme!(theme_amber_light())
```

A Bode plot answers how much a circuit amplifies and shifts each frequency. A
Nyquist plot shows the same complex response as a path in the complex plane.
AmberMakie can place both views in one figure without recomputing the analysis.

```{julia}
@circuit MakieLowPass(; R=10kΩ, C=10nF) begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=0V, ac=1V)
    R1 = resistor(input, output; value=R)
    C1 = capacitor(output, gnd; value=C)
end

response = small_signal(MakieLowPass(), 10Hz => 1MHz;
    source=:Source, points=301, scale=:log)
view = frequencyview(response;
    input=voltage(:input), output=voltage(:output));
```

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(1100, 600))
bodeplot(figure[1, 1], response;
    input=voltage(:input), output=voltage(:output), color="#0072B2")
nyquistplot(figure[1, 2], view; color="#D55E00")
Label(figure[0, :], "RC low-pass in two coordinate systems"; fontsize=20)
figure
```

The numerical result remains available beside the plot. Here we find the
sample nearest the analytic pole and print the values a reader should expect
to see.

```{julia}
expected_corner = inv(2π * 10kΩ * 10nF)
i = argmin(abs.(view.frequencies .- expected_corner))

(
    expected_corner_hz=expected_corner,
    sampled_frequency_hz=view.frequencies[i],
    gain_db=20log10(abs(view.response[i])),
    phase_degrees=rad2deg(angle(view.response[i])),
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
Both views describe the small-signal linearization around the operating point.
Clipping and slew-rate limits require a transient analysis.
:::
